quizName:
DMV Practice Test  #9
										  					
  

25 Questions • Passing Score 20

questions.question: The posted speed limit is the fastest you can legally drive in an area.

options.text: True
False

questions.correctAnswerText: True
questions.explanation: The posted speed limit is the fastest legal speed under good conditions. You must drive slower when conditions are bad, such as wet roads or poor visibility.

questions.question: A regulatory sign with a red circle and slash means:

options.text: Come to a complete stop.
An action is forbidden.
Some drivers must yield to others.
Drive below the speed limit.

questions.correctAnswerText: An action is forbidden.
questions.explanation: A red circle with a slash on a sign means that action is not allowed. These signs are white with red and black markings. The red circle and slash shows that the action is forbidden.

questions.question: This road sign means:

options.text: Drive with caution and be ready to slow down.
Do not drive in this lane.
Come to a complete stop and yield the right-of-way.
Slow down, be ready to stop, and yield the right-of-way if needed.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down, be ready to stop, and yield the right-of-way if needed.
questions.explanation: This triangular sign means you must yield. Slow down at the intersection, be ready to stop, and let other vehicles, bicycles, and pedestrians pass safely before you go.

questions.question: What should you do if your vehicle's right wheels leave the pavement?

options.text: Stop quickly.
Pull all the way off the road and get back on when safe.
Speed up and steer back quickly.
Release the gas pedal, slow down, then gently steer back onto the road when safe.

questions.correctAnswerText: Release the gas pedal, slow down, then gently steer back onto the road when safe.
questions.explanation: Don't panic if your right wheels leave the pavement. Release the gas and steer parallel to the road. Slow down and gently steer back with both hands on the wheel using a small turn. Check for traffic before steering back onto the road.

questions.question: A learner's permit allows a new driver to drive while supervised by:

options.text: A licensed parent, legal guardian, driving instructor, or another adult who has signed for financial responsibility.
Any licensed driver.
A licensed driving instructor only.
Any driver over age 21.

questions.correctAnswerText: A licensed parent, legal guardian, driving instructor, or another adult who has signed for financial responsibility.
questions.explanation: With a learner's permit, you must have an approved driving instructor, parent, or legal guardian with you. A responsible licensed adult who signed for financial responsibility can also supervise.

questions.question: You may drive around or under a railroad crossing gate that is being lowered or raised:

options.text: As long as a train is not too close.
If your vehicle will not damage the gate.
If you look both ways first.
Never.

questions.correctAnswerText: Never.
questions.explanation: Flashing red lights, lowered gates, and bells at railroad crossings mean you must stop completely. Do not cross the tracks until the lights and bells stop and the gates are fully up. Never drive around or under a moving gate.

questions.question: Space between your vehicle and others is important because it:

options.text: Prevents distractions from other vehicles.
Gives you time to react to unexpected situations.
Keeps traffic moving at a safe speed.
Keeps other drivers alert.

questions.correctAnswerText: Gives you time to react to unexpected situations.
questions.explanation: Leave plenty of space between you and other vehicles so you have time to react if another driver makes a mistake.

questions.question: When you see or hear an emergency vehicle coming, you should:

options.text: Stop right away and let the vehicle pass.
Move as far right as safely possible and stop.
Drive slowly and let the vehicle pass.
Keep moving slowly on the right side of the road.

questions.correctAnswerText: Move as far right as safely possible and stop.
questions.explanation: When an emergency vehicle uses lights and/or sirens, you must yield no matter which direction it comes from. Move as close as safely possible to the right side of the road and stop. Do not stop in an intersection.

questions.question: You do not need as much distance when following a motorcycle as when following a car.

options.text: True
False

questions.correctAnswerText: False
questions.explanation: Motorcycles can stop faster than cars in dry conditions. Stay at least three to four seconds behind a motorcycle so the rider has time to react in an emergency.

questions.question: If you need to slow down on a slippery road, the first thing you should do is:

options.text: Apply the brakes firmly.
Take your foot off the gas pedal.
Use the parking brake.
Pump the brakes.

questions.correctAnswerText: Take your foot off the gas pedal.
questions.explanation: To slow down on a slippery road, first release the gas pedal. If you need to slow more, gently press the brake pedal with steady, light pressure.

questions.question: When driving on wet pavement, remember:

options.text: Roads are especially slippery right after rain starts.
Wet roads can cause hydroplaning.
Leave extra space when stopping.
All of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: All of the above.
questions.explanation: Wet roads are very slippery, especially right after it rains. Your tires ride on a layer of water, oil, and dirt. Slow down when there is rain, standing water, or slush to keep your wheels from sliding.

questions.question: When dealing with pedestrians, a driver must:

options.text: Make sure the pedestrian sees your vehicle.
Always yield the right-of-way, even if the pedestrian is wrong.
Yield only when the pedestrian has the legal right-of-way.
Slow down and honk near a crosswalk.

questions.correctAnswerText: Always yield the right-of-way, even if the pedestrian is wrong.
questions.explanation: Do everything possible to avoid hitting a pedestrian or another vehicle, no matter what. It is your responsibility to watch for pedestrians and yield to them, even if they are crossing illegally.

questions.question: When driving on an interstate:

options.text: Stop on the shoulder if you are tired.
You should always use cruise control.
Signal, check mirrors, and check blind spots before changing lanes.
You should change lanes often.

questions.correctAnswerText: Signal, check mirrors, and check blind spots before changing lanes.
questions.explanation: Signal, check your mirrors, and check your blind spot before changing lanes or passing. Only stop on the shoulder for emergencies. Change lanes as little as possible. Do not use cruise control in heavy traffic or bad weather.

questions.question: A person who drives much slower than the speed limit:

options.text: Is a very safe driver.
Always has the right-of-way.
Should not let following cars pass.
May create a dangerous driving environment.

questions.correctAnswerText: May create a dangerous driving environment.
questions.explanation: Driving much slower than traffic around you is dangerous. If you are on a two-lane road and cars are backing up behind you, pull over and let them pass. Only drive well below the speed limit when road conditions require it.

questions.question: You are approaching a railroad crossing with a crossbuck sign but no gates or flashing lights. You should:

options.text: Approach with caution and cross only when you are sure no train is coming.
Turn down your radio to listen for an approaching train.
Only continue when a flagger signals you to cross, if present.
All of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: All of the above.
questions.explanation: Approach all railroad crossings carefully and cross only when you know no train is coming. If a flagger is present, follow their instructions.

questions.question: What do speed limit signs show?

options.text: Possible speeds for the area
The maximum or minimum speed you can legally drive
The speed to drive in heavy traffic
The speed to drive in bad weather

questions.correctAnswerText: The maximum or minimum speed you can legally drive
questions.explanation: Speed limit signs show the maximum or minimum safe speed allowed on a road. The maximum limits are for ideal conditions. You must slow down when conditions are not ideal.

questions.question: As a pedestrian, you should:

options.text: Always demand the right-of-way over vehicles in a crosswalk.
Never enter a street or crosswalk when vehicles are approaching.
Enter a crosswalk anytime because drivers must stop.
Use crosswalks only if convenient.

questions.correctAnswerText: Never enter a street or crosswalk when vehicles are approaching.
questions.explanation: Do not enter a street or crosswalk when vehicles are approaching. Even though pedestrians have the right-of-way in crosswalks, a vehicle that is close may not be able to stop in time.

questions.question: Drive below the posted speed limit when:

options.text: Anything makes conditions less than perfect.
You see a police car.
You are entering a highway with other cars.
You are on a four-lane road.

questions.correctAnswerText: Anything makes conditions less than perfect.
questions.explanation: Drive below the speed limit when roads are wet or slippery, visibility is poor, or anything else makes conditions unsafe. You can be ticketed for speeding even if you are within the posted limit when conditions are bad.

questions.question: A good defensive driver:

options.text: Always drives slowly.
Watches what other drivers do.
Travels at a constant speed.
Only drives in familiar areas.

questions.correctAnswerText: Watches what other drivers do.
questions.explanation: A defensive driver watches for what other drivers are doing and prepares for possible problems. Even experienced drivers can get distracted.

questions.question: You are in the right lane of a multilane highway and want to move to the left lane. You should:

options.text: Check your rearview mirror for traffic behind you before changing lanes.
Look over your left shoulder for traffic in your blind spot before changing lanes.
Check your side mirror for traffic and turn on your turn signal.
All of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: All of the above.
questions.explanation: Before changing lanes, check your mirrors and look over your shoulder to make sure no vehicles are in the lane you want to enter. Always signal when you change lanes.

questions.question: When a driver behind you wants to pass, what should you do?

options.text: Speed up.
Keep the same speed.
Slow down to give the other driver room to pass safely.
Change lanes.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down to give the other driver room to pass safely.
questions.explanation: When a driver behind you wants to pass, slow down. This gives them enough space in front of your car to pass quickly and safely.

questions.question: What does a single dashed yellow line in the center of the road mean?

options.text: You may pass if it is safe to do so.
Both lanes go in the same direction.
You may not pass.
You may pass, even if it is dangerous.

questions.correctAnswerText: You may pass if it is safe to do so.
questions.explanation: A single dashed yellow line means traffic moves in opposite directions. You may pass only if it is safe and you will not interfere with oncoming traffic.

questions.question: Which statement about speed is true?

options.text: Driving too slowly on certain highways can be dangerous.
Speeding can kill.
Speeding is not dangerous if you are a skilled driver.
Both A and B are true.

questions.correctAnswerText: Both A and B are true.
questions.explanation: Higher speeds increase the risk of death in a crash. Driving much slower than other traffic is also dangerous because other drivers may make risky moves to pass you.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: There is an object on the road.
Traffic is coming from the right.
The road curves sharply to the left.
There is a merge point ahead.

questions.correctAnswerText: The road curves sharply to the left.
questions.explanation: Chevron signs warn of sharp curves. The arrow shows the direction of the curve. You may see several of these signs placed along the curve.

questions.question: How can you avoid crashes when driving on ice or snow?

options.text: Add extra weight to your vehicle for better grip.
Leave the highways as soon as possible.
Use four-wheel drive.
Slow down and stay farther behind other cars.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down and stay farther behind other cars.
questions.explanation: On snowy or icy roads, reduce your speed and increase the distance between you and other cars. These are the most important ways to avoid crashes in bad weather.
